docs.title: Welcome to InferDoc
docs.text: InferDoc is an AI-powered GitHub Action that automatically generates and updates comprehensive documentation for your Python projects.

docs.title: 🚀 Features
docs.text:
• Automatic Documentation Generation: Parses your Python codebase and generates beautiful documentation
  • AI-Powered Docstrings: Uses GPT-4o-mini to generate missing docstrings automatically
  • Git History Integration: Analyzes commit history to provide "Recent Changes" summaries
  • Beautiful UI: Generates modern, searchable documentation using MkDocs Material theme
  • GitHub Actions Integration: Automatically updates documentation on every push
  • Zero Configuration: Works out of the box with sensible defaults

docs.title: 🎯 How It Works
docs.text:
1. Parse: InferDoc analyzes your Python files using AST (Abstract Syntax Tree)
  2. Enhance: Missing docstrings are automatically generated using AI
  3. Analyze: Git commit history is summarized for each file
  4. Generate: Beautiful Markdown documentation is created
  5. Deploy: Documentation is automatically deployed to GitHub Pages

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/Om7035/InferDoc.git
cd InferDoc

# Create virtual environment
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: .\venv\Scripts\activate

# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
1. Create a .env file with your OpenAI API key: 

    cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env and add your OPENAI_API_KEY

  2. Run locally on a single file: 

    python run_local.py

  3. Preview the documentation: 

    mkdocs serve

Visit http://127.0.0.1:8000 to see your documentation!

docs.title: 🔧 Components
docs.text:
InferDoc consists of four main components:

  • Parser (parser.py): Extracts structure from Python files using AST
  • Generator (generator.py): Transforms parsed data into Markdown using Jinja2
  • AI Enhancer (ai_enhancer.py): Generates missing docstrings using OpenAI
  • Git Analyzer (git_analyzer.py): Summarizes commit history for each file

docs.title: Function: generate_markdown(structure, template_dir, template_name, module_name, summary)
docs.text:
Docstring: 

Generate Markdown documentation from a parsed structure using a Jinja2 template.

Args:
    structure: Parsed structure dictionary from parser.parse_python_file()
    template_dir: Directory containing Jinja2 templates
    template_name: Name of the template file to use
    module_name: Name of the module being documented
    summary: Optional summary text (e.g., from git analysis)

Returns:
    str: Generated Markdown content

Raises:
    TemplateNotFound: If the specified template does not exist
    Exception: If template rendering fails

Example:
    >>> structure = parse_python_file('my_module.py')
    >>> markdown = generate_markdown(
    ...     structure,
    ...     'templates',
    ...     'module.md.j2',
    ...     'my_module.py',
    ...     'Recent updates to error handling'
    ... )
    >>> print(markdown)

docs.title: Function: parse_python_file(file_path)
docs.text:
Docstring: 

Parse a Python file and extract its structure.

This function analyzes a Python source file and extracts information about
all classes and functions defined in it, including their docstrings,
arguments, and source code.

Args:
    file_path: Path to the Python file to parse

Returns:
    dict: A dictionary containing two keys:
        - 'classes': List of class information dictionaries
        - 'functions': List of function information dictionaries

Raises:
    FileNotFoundError: If the specified file does not exist
    SyntaxError: If the file contains invalid Python syntax

Example:
    >>> structure = parse_python_file('my_module.py')
    >>> print(f"Found {len(structure['classes'])} classes")
    >>> print(f"Found {len(structure['functions'])} functions")
